clue.text: Sid turns up with Daisy, a calamity!

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the name taken as written, before it is turned
the aster, or Michaelmas daisy, is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A man called Sid arrives with a woman called Daisy, and it goes horribly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a woman's name, but it is the flower: DIS plus ASTER gives DISASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden event causing great damage or misfortune, which is exactly what a calamity is.

clue.text: Sounds like they're ringing beautiful women

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the answer is said the same as another word

parts.note: things that ring are bells; the spelling for lovely women is said identically

explanation.surface: Some lovely women seem to have a voice like chimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired one at a party or in a town.

clue.text: What nurses use when the musicians take a long time?

parts.note: a group of musicians playing together
informally, ages means a very long time

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about hospital supplies whenever the band is slow to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurses wrap wounds in strips of gauze or cloth, the dressings they apply to injuries.

clue.text: An ice cream container

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Britain, an ice cream served in a wafer cone
second meaning: a cone-shaped paper bag for holding sweets or nuts

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a cone; the clue splits into two senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: British English calls a wafer cone with ice cream in it a cornet, and also a twisted paper cone used to hold sweets.

clue.text: Girl wanted to help men outside

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it, with the other sitting within

parts.note: taken as written; this is the outer word
to aid is to help

explanation.surface: A job advert: a young woman is wanted to assist some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanted' reads as part of the advert, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old-fashioned or poetic word for a young unmarried woman or girl.

clue.text: Sorrow of skinflint at the end of the day

parts.note: a skinflint is a stingy person, a miser

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

parts.note: the final letter of the second word

explanation.surface: A stingy person feels gloomy when the working day is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is great unhappiness or distress, a close synonym of deep sorrow or grief.

clue.text: What prisoner may be given if father takes part?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
an actor's part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: Musing over whether a convict gets an early release when Dad plays along.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is the conditional early release of a prisoner, granted on promise of good behaviour.

clue.text: Going around Rolls-Royce, poor Rose slips

indicators.note: going around something means surrounding it on both sides
something in poor shape has fallen apart, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the name taken as written, to be rearranged
RR is the standard abbreviation for Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: Poor Rose keeps slipping up while driving round a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is rearranged first, and the result then wraps around the car's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, so slips are minor errors or blunders.

clue.text: Firework which lit up a room in the Italian capital?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a firework that shoots out balls of coloured fire

definitions.text: which lit up a room in the Italian capital
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase, read literally as a light used in Rome
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: a candle from Rome used for indoor light

explanation.walkthrough: The second half invites you to picture an actual candle in a house in Rome, the literal reading of the firework's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube-shaped firework that ejects a series of flaming stars is called by this name; literally it is a candle from the city of Rome.

clue.text: When to go to sea and attack

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to sail is to travel over the sea in a boat

explanation.surface: Pirates choose the moment to put out to sea and launch an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, physically or with words, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Turning dry air on is nothing special

indicators.note: turning things over and around mixes up their order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all eight letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Switching on a dehumidifier is a mundane, unremarkable act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary is common and unremarkable, without any special or distinctive features.

clue.text: Courage? King George needs it

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, Latin for King George
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether the king requires bravery to face what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: GR appears as a royal cipher on British postboxes from the reigns of the King Georges.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is informal for strength of character and determination, much like bravery or pluck.

clue.text: Butchers chuckling in a ship

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed within it

parts.note: SS means steamship, the prefix before a ship's name
chuckling is a form of laughter

explanation.surface: Meat cutters sharing a joke aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Butchers is a verb here, not the tradesmen: LAUGHTER sits inside S...S.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to kill brutally or in large numbers, just as to slaughter is.

clue.text: Radio personality on board spilt some sugar

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered out of place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
caster sugar is a fine white sugar used in British baking

explanation.surface: A DJ on a ship knocks over the sugar bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster presents programmes on radio or television, so is a familiar on-air personality.

clue.text: Moving chair can, causing chaos

indicators.note: moving things around shifts their places, so these letters change order

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Shifting furniture and a tin around makes a real mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic describes disorder with no control or rules, the lawless state that produces chaos.

clue.text: Civil Engineer standing still, enraptured

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for Civil Engineer
static means motionless or still

explanation.surface: An engineer stands motionless, completely carried away with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing still' wants to be a single phrase; 'standing' turns CE up into EC, and 'still' alone gives STATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enraptured means filled with intense joy or delight, the state of overwhelming happiness that ecstatic describes.

clue.text: Boy in the SAS getting healthy meals?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that these dishes are only sometimes full meals

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits within it

parts.note: the Special Air Service, a British army regiment, taken as written
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A young recruit to the special forces is fed well.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS (Special Air Service) is an elite British army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Salads are dishes of raw vegetables or leaves, widely seen as nutritious, light food.

clue.text: Develop and go round topless!

indicators.note: without a top, so in a down clue the first letter is cut off

parts.note: to revolve is to turn around a centre

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to grow up and then dance around with no shirt on.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually, the way species or ideas change over time.

clue.text: Leading volunteers taking home journalist to be looked after

parts.note: main means chief or leading
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
being in means being at home
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Top volunteers take a reporter back to their house to care for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something maintained is kept in good condition and cared for, so looked after in the sense of upkeep.

clue.text: Fool silly twin with it

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behave foolishly and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling a sibling an idiot for being daft.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is an informal term for a stupid or silly person, an idiot or dunce.

clue.text: Swing end of rod to try to catch fish

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler swings the tip of the fishing rod hoping for a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle is to hang loosely and sway, so swing is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Rescue, in rough seas, a vessel

parts.note: surface padding only, describing the sea

indicators.note: the answer is said to be in the words that follow, sitting inside them unaltered

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, the middle word and the first two of the last

explanation.surface: A rescue of a boat caught in stormy waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' is only scenery; nothing is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone is to rescue them from danger or harm.

clue.text: Unusual in a cult, a marine

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of their ordinary order

parts.note: all eight letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier from the sea has odd membership of a sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' looks like a noun for a soldier, but it is the adjective meaning of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives relate to the sea, ships and sailing, so marine and nautical are synonyms.

clue.text: Almost noon before it should be?

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for noon
early means ahead of the proper time

explanation.surface: Wondering whether it is nearly midday ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost both mean very close to but not quite, so they are interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Ghost coming out of the drinks cabinet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a supernatural being, an apparition

definitions.text: coming out of the drinks cabinet
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for an alcoholic drink rather than a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a strong distilled drink such as gin or whisky

explanation.walkthrough: The surface imagines a phantom emerging from the cupboard; the second half really describes a bottle of liquor poured from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A disembodied soul or apparition is one sense; distilled liquor like brandy or vodka is the other sense of the same word.

clue.text: Spot in which I found fish

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a location where someone discovered a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside PLACE, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flat European sea fish, popular in British fish and chip shops.
